basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 16.' and it opens 'Vers. 16. Hoc erit velamen oculorum. Id est: in funeris praeparatione: Mementoque te'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 16. Hoc erit velamen oculorum. Id est: in funeris praeparatione: Mementoque te deprehensam. Hoc quasi jocando dicit monens eam amabiliter ne hoc auderet facere, ne similiter deprehensa videretur. Mystice loco hoc Abraham Christum significat, Sara vero Ecclesiam. Abraham honorabatur propter Sarae pulchritudinem et Christus laudatur in mundo et honoratur per Ecclesiam; quia sicut Psalmista dicit: Mirabilis Deus in sanctis suis (Ps. XVII, 36). Habebat Sara virum, sed latebat, et Ecclesia habet Christum, sed videtur in praesenti receptus secretis coelestibus.
